description: EquipRite Next: designed from the FDD, on the same services as Old (webApps/vbredwoodapp) and New (webApps/equiprite), which are not changed.

featureFlags.description: App-wide feature-flag map { SETTING_KEY: 'true'|'false' } loaded once at app start from EQR_CONF_EQUIPMENT_SETTING (SETTING_CATEGORY='FEATURE_FLAG'). Flags are APPLICATION-LEVEL (not BU-scoped). Read via $application.functions.isFeatureEnabled(key). Backend enforces the hard rule; this drives UX (show-but-disabled).

flagsLoaded.description: True once loadFeatureFlagsChain has populated featureFlags AND globalSettings. isFeatureEnabled() / isQuotingAllowed() fail CLOSED (return false) until this is true.

globalSettings.description: App-wide non-boolean global settings map { SETTING_KEY: 'value' } loaded once at app start from EQR_CONF_GLOBAL_SETTINGS (SETTING_CATEGORY='SYSTEM'), alongside featureFlags. Separate from featureFlags because these are enums/strings, not 'true'|'false' — isFeatureEnabled() is the wrong accessor for them. Holds ENABLE_QUOTES (NONE|PROJECTS|CUSTOMER|BOTH), read via $application.functions.isQuotingAllowed(). Gated by the same flagsLoaded latch.

buRateSources.description: Per-BU rate source { businessUnitId: 'PPM_RATES'|'EQUIPRITE_RATES' } from EQR_CONF_EQUIPMENT_SETTING.RATE_SOURCE, built by buRateSourceMap. Loaded in loadFeatureFlagsChain BEFORE flagsLoaded flips, and refreshed by the Configurations BU Settings loader after a save. Read only through usesPpmRates() / isRateManagementHidden(), which apply the hierarchy: PPM_RATES_ENABLED ON overrides every BU; OFF lets each BU decide.

ppmCostRateScheduleName.description: EXACT name of the Fusion PPM nonlabor COST rate schedule to read units from (e.g. 'OII AE Nonlabor Cost Rate AED'). Required because NOTHING in Fusion's data marks a schedule as cost vs bill -- both are ScheduleType 'Nonlabor' and the distinction lives in the organization costing rule, which REST does not expose. The name also separates the currency pair: a tenant holds an AED schedule and a USD one over the same lines, so a prefix match would pick a currency at random. CURRENTLY SET TO A dev20 TEST VALUE ('UK Non Labor Cost Rate'), chosen because it is the richest nonlabor cost schedule on that pod (6 lines) and it carries Equipment -> Hours, and 'Equipment' is one of the four values the picker always offers -- so the unit lookup demonstrably hits. dev20 has NO Day-based lines, so the 1-per-day cap cannot be exercised there; the customer's own pod is overwhelmingly Day. THIS BELONGS IN CONFIGURATION, not in a shipped default -- move it to EQR_CONF_GLOBAL_SETTINGS when the backend lands. BLANK DISABLES EVERYTHING: no unit lookup runs and the timesheet behaves exactly as it did before units existed -- the Expenditure Type picker keeps its project-scoped list, the hours cap stays 24, and nothing is cleared on a type change. Set it only once the schedule name is confirmed on the pod. Consumed by resources/js/fusionRateLines.js via the timesheet's vbEnterChain.

jwt.description: Access token passed in on the launch URL (?jwt=...). loadFusionRolesChain decodes its payload and uses the `sub` claim as the Fusion username for the ROLES_RP BIP call, in preference to $application.user — sub is the account the token was issued for, whereas the VB identity object is inconsistently populated in this environment. OPTIONAL: absent or undecodable, the chain falls back to $application.user exactly as before, so nothing depends on the URL carrying it. DECODED, NOT VERIFIED — the browser has no signing key, so this is a claim rather than a proven identity; it is acceptable only because the roles it yields are a UX gate and the backend independently authorizes every request. Never treat a jwt-derived role as authorization.

fusionRoles.description: The signed-in user's FUSION job role codes (e.g. ORA_OSS_SUBSCRIPTION_SPECIALIST_JOB), fetched from the ROLES_RP BIP report by loadFusionRolesChain. Needed because $application.user.roles carries only VB Studio platform roles in this environment and no ORA_*_JOB code. Empty = no roles resolved = every page HIDDEN (fail-closed).

pageAccessMap.description: Page-level RBAC map { PAGE_CODE: 'FULL'|'READ_ONLY'|'HIDDEN' } resolved once at app start by loadPageAccessChain from COMMONRITE RBAC (APPLICATION_CODE='EQUIP_RITE') for the signed-in user's Fusion job role. THE single source for both the nav-menu filter and the page-entry guard, so they can never disagree. A page code absent from this map resolves to HIDDEN (fail-closed). UX layer only — the backend enforces independently.

pageAccessLoaded.description: SETTLED latch: true once loadPageAccessChain has finished, whatever the outcome. On success pageAccessMap holds the role's grants; on no role, an unmapped role or a failed call it stays {} and every page resolves to HIDDEN, so the guards send the user to the No Access page. false therefore means STILL LOADING and nothing else (canEnterPage admits during that window; the shell's recheckPageAccessChain re-checks once it settles). The nav menu stays empty until this is true.

sessionRoles.description: The signed-in user's EquipRite SESSION_ROLE codes (EQUIP_MGR, REQUESTOR, ...), ordered by RBAC_ROLE_MAP priority (lower first), resolved by loadPageAccessChain from GET /rbac/session-roles. This is what makes the dashboard persona and the manager-tier checks table-driven: a customer whose Fusion roles are named differently (OII_RT_EQP_MANAGER_JR) needs only RBAC_ROLE_MAP rows, no code change. Empty = not resolved (call failed, endpoint not deployed, or nothing mapped); the role functions then fall back to the hard-coded RT_EQP_* map in app-flow.js. Includes legacy roles with no dashboard (ADMIN, EQUIP_MANAGER); consumers pick the first code they recognise.

sessionRolesLoaded.description: SETTLED latch for sessionRoles: true once loadPageAccessChain's session-role lookup has finished, whether it succeeded, failed or was skipped. Pages wait on it (bounded) so they resolve the persona from the server list rather than the fallback map. NOT a fail-closed gate: false and true-with-empty both mean 'use the fallback'.

commonLookups.description: Shared reference-data cache { LOOKUP_TYPE: [{value,label}] } loaded once at app start by loadCommonLookupsChain from COMMONRITE.RS_LOOKUP_VALUES (APPLICATION_CODE='EQUIP_RITE', ENABLED_FLAG='Y', language 'en'). That table is shared across I9_ADMIN / ONBOARD_RITE / TALENT_TRACKER / EQUIP_RITE, so the application_code scope is an isolation boundary rather than a filter. Read via $application.functions.getLookupLabel(type, code) and getLookupOptions(type). UNLIKE featureFlags and pageAccessMap this is DISPLAY DATA and does NOT fail closed: an empty map means labels fall back to the hardcoded map in resources/js/lineStatusLabels.js, never a blocked UI.

lookupsLoaded.description: True once loadCommonLookupsChain has populated commonLookups; also serves as that chain's re-entry cache check. Accessors degrade GRACEFULLY (caller fallback, else the raw code) while this is false. This is deliberately NOT the fail-closed contract used by flagsLoaded and pageAccessLoaded — a dead lookups service must never hide functionality, so do not write a gate against this latch.

appUrls.description: Where Old, New and Next EquipRite live, for the toolbar's switch. Set by loadVersionsChain: from the desktop app's /__versions locally, or under VBCS by swapping webApps/equiprite-next for webApps/vbredwoodapp and webApps/equiprite in this page's address. Empty until known; the switch then shows only Next.

viewAs.description: The persona My work is shown as (an administrator may look at any persona's work). Empty: the user's own.
